definition: A model that assigns probabilities to sequences of words, typically based on statistical patterns like word co-occurrence frequencies, predating neural language models.
details: Statistical language models, including n-gram models, were the standard approach in NLP for decades before neural network-based language models became dominant with the rise of deep learning.

explainer.lead: A statistical language model assigns probabilities to sequences of words from patterns such as co-occurrence frequencies. It matters as the foundation that neural language models later displaced.

tiers.eli5: It guesses how likely a phrase is by how often its words tend to appear together in text you have seen.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use n-gram models where speed and simplicity matter. A pitfall is that they capture limited context and generalize poorly beyond observed patterns.
tiers.paperLevel: The model assigns probabilities to word sequences based on statistical patterns like co-occurrence frequencies; n-gram models are the canonical form. They were the standard NLP approach for decades before neural models dominated.

explainer.example: An n-gram model scores a sentence by multiplying the frequencies of each short word sequence it contains.
